thread.title: Stocks Rally A Bit After Monday Sell-Off; Netflix Leads FANG Rebound

author: EdJenner
title: Stocks Rally A Bit After Monday Sell-Off; Netflix Leads FANG Rebound
text:
Stocks were slightly higher near midday Tuesday, a disappointing performance for the bulls after Monday’s drubbing that saw leading growth stocks come under heavy selling pressure.
X
Leaderboard name Netflix ( NFLX ) rebounded 3.5% after Monday’s 6.5% haircut. It was by far the best performer among the FANG stocks. Other top gainers in the Nasdaq 100 included IBD 50 name Align Technology ( ALGN ), Lam Research ( LRCX ), Micron ( MU ) and Apple ( AAPL ).
Apple is testing support at its 50-day moving average, while UBS upgraded shares of Lam Research and Micron.
The Dow Jones industrial average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq composite were all up around 0.2%. Volume on the NYSE and Nasdaq was tracking lower than Monday’s levels.
In stock market results today , Akamai ( AKAM ) gapped below its 50-day moving average, falling 3%, after the company forecast second-quarter earnings and sales at the low end of prior guidance. Stocks On The Move
Among retailers, At Home ( HOME ) gapped up to a new high, rising 6%. Morgan Stanley upgraded shares to overweight from equal weight.
Stitch Fix ( SFIX ) recovered nearly half of Monday’s 11% decline. The new issue’s chart is still intact as it trades just below its recent high of 30.07. It’s plenty liquid with an average daily volume of around 1.7 million shares, but annual earnings growth is expected to slow this year, falling 41% to 19 cents a share. The company earned 32 cents in 2017.
A couple of China-based IBD 50 names bounced back after Monday’s drubbing that saw the IBD 50 index drop 3.3%. Baozun ( BZUN ) rallied nearly 3% after paying a visit to its 50-day line Monday. Gold lost ground again as the U.S. dollar strengthened. After hitting a high of 129.47 on April 11, SPDR Gold Shares ( GLD ) is down nearly 8%. The exchanged-traded fund fell another 0.3% to 119.48. It’s still holding above its December low of 117.40.
